question: Is macro R2(B) < macro R2(A) an artefact of penalising the covariate block, given that B's design matrix contains A's?
decides_nothing_about: whether the encoder representation has phenotype value
whether the biological hierarchy adds anything
evaluation: group-5-fold cross-validation over the pooled development individuals, families kept whole

specification_notes.S1: every column standardized, one alpha over [covariates | dosage]; reproduces run_stage2b.fit_ridge_predictions and tqg1_core.fit_ridge
specification_notes.S2: covariates unpenalized, dosage penalized, fitted jointly (partial ridge via Frisch-Waugh-Lovell)
specification_notes.S3: covariates fitted by OLS, dosage ridged on the residual (standard two-stage eQTL recipe)

primary_readout: macro R2(B) - macro R2(A) per specification at snps_per_gene=256

decision_rule.artefact_supported: B-A > 0 with CI95 excluding 0 under S2 and S3, while S1's B-A stays at or below 0
decision_rule.artefact_refuted: B-A does not clear 0 under any specification
decision_rule.note: a diagnostic outcome, not a gate; neither branch reopens or overturns a frozen pilot

interpretation_limits: development individuals only; task_gate and bridge_test are never read
cross-validated within development, so this is not a held-out replication
gene panel and cis selection are inherited from TQ-G1 so that the fit specification is the only thing that varies
uniform thinning is kept deliberately, so a null here does not rule out that lead cis-eQTLs are simply absent from the panel
this diagnostic cannot overturn the frozen TQ-G1 verdict and does not evaluate any encoder arm
